event.observed: The source explicitly declared YYYY-MM-DD and supplied 2026-04-05. A locale-based fallback reversed the month and day and represented the value as 4 May 2026. The implemented correction used the existing strict YYYY-MM-DD parsing procedure instead of that fallback.
event.outcome: Parsing by the declared format produced year=2026, month=4 and day=5: 5 April 2026. The original input text was retained. No additional date format or new parsing rule was introduced.

event.observed: The source explicitly declared comma-separated CSV with double-quote quoting. For the data row Ada,"x,y", a naive split on commas produced three fragments: ["Ada","\"x","y\""]. The implemented correction used the existing structural CSV parser with the declared comma delimiter and double-quote quoting.
event.outcome: The parser returned exactly two field values: ["Ada","x,y"]. The quoted comma remained inside the second field, and field values and row association were preserved. No additional delimiter, quoting convention or field-name mapping was introduced.
